source: Six learner attempts saved as one batch
lessonTheme: Practical affirmative tú commands and esto/esta contrast
summary: Learner explicitly requested practical imperatives. Introduced regular affirmative tú -ar → -a and -er → -e, with revisa, crea and lee. All five full-sentence attempts used the right command verb after models. Esto before función recurred twice; correct esta in a cued gap followed by correct Revisa esto por favor. Separate command success from demonstrative errors and spelling.

observations.outcome: Affirmative tú command revisa correctly formed after a model and regular -ar explanation. Esto before función corrected to esta; accent supplied.
Correct crea after crear → crea was provided. Una capitalization and función accent supplied. Tutor then introduced regular -er imperative ending -e with leer → lee.

Correct lee after leer → lee explanation. For the practised general Read this target tutor supplied esto. Esta alone can refer to a known feminine item in other contexts; do not label the raw sentence universally ungrammatical.
Correct lee retained, but esto before función recurred and needed esta. Tutor narrowed practice to an esto/esta choice rather than adding another command rule.
Correct cued choice esta for Revisa ___ función, por favor. Recognition with two options, not independent full-sentence production.

Correct full review-this command after feminine-noun gap practice. Correctly switched to standalone esto. Immediate prompted transfer; punctuation was modelled in feedback, with no grammatical correction.

nextSteps: Recheck full esta función production after intervening material
Recall revisa, crea and lee without a fresh model
Keep new command units practical and individually skippable
Later introduce one further command pattern at a time
assessmentNote: Model-supported commands, cued demonstrative recognition and immediate full-sentence transfer are recorded separately. No long-term retention claim.
